title: String-comparison against "href" + "xlink:href"

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitize-core, step 1.5.9.5.3 reads:

>  "If the [built-in animating URL attributes list](https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#built-in-animating-url-attributes-list) [contains](https://wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api/#sanitizerconfig-contains) «[elementName, attrName]» and attr’s [value](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-get-value) [is](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-is) "href" or "xlink:href", then [remove](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-remove) attribute."

https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-element-setattributens, step 1, calls ["validate and extract"](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#validate-and-extract), which reads:

> 4. If qualifiedName contains a U+003A (:):
>    1. Let splitResult be the result of running [strictly split](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strictly-split) given qualifiedName and U+003A (:).
>    [...]
>    3. Set localName to splitResult[1].

For a qualifiedName "xlink:href:abc", this would set localName to "href". The ":abc" is discarded. Blink implements this as specified:

```js
d = document.createElement("div");
d.setAttributeNS("https://www.w3.org/1999/xlink", "xlink:href:abc", "https://www.example.org");
d.attributes[0]  // xlink.href="https://www.example.org"
d.attributes[0].localName  // "href"
```

[SVG Animations](https://svgwg.org/specs/animations/) is [surprisingly vague](https://svgwg.org/specs/animations/#TargetAttributes) about what the `attributeName` value means. I guess in XML-world it didn't have to. Blink has implemented `<svg:set attributeName>` to also use "validate and extract" to parse its value as a qualified name, so that `<svg:set attributeName="xlink:href:abc">` would animate the target element's `href` attribute. This is rather surprising and, worse, is a bypass of the Sanitizer API guarantees.

By my reading, Blink's implementation matches the specs. Admittedly, with the rather large caveat that it's not particularly clear how SVG, or actually SVG-in-HTML-syntax, wants `attributeName` to be interpreted. If my reading of the spec is correct, then the string comparison in "sanitizer core" is insufficient.

-----  

Original report [here](https://g-issues.chromium.org/issues/487863654).
